evidence: The adapter passes exactly 30000 to AbortSignal.timeout.
The timeout remains attached to the single strict, stateless, tool-free Responses request.
Configured server credential, model, prompt version, strict schema, and store false behavior are unchanged.
All nine bounded failure classes preserve conversation state and create no decision audit or authorized consequence.
Provider rejection details are discarded and classified as opaque HTTP failure.
An operational observer exception cannot change the bounded safe response or preservation command.
The operational payload has exactly the keys event and failureClass.
The event name is the fixed literal decision_failure and failureClass is restricted to the nine-class union.
The event contains no owner input, provider output or error, Telegram update or user identifier, token, credential, trace, or chain of thought.
The production logger receives only that allowlisted payload.
Telegram update identity is claimed before conversation or provider execution, so concurrent retry of the same update is stopped before the engine and produces no second reply.

residual_timing_risk: A provider response slower than thirty seconds still fails closed as timeout.
The longer bound increases webhook latency and can overlap a Telegram retry; the durable pre-engine update claim suppresses duplicate processing.
Deployed provider latency and Telegram delivery still require S01-12 release evidence; this QA made no external request or mutation.
execution_note: The first full-gate attempt was denied localhost binding by the QA sandbox. The exact command was rerun with localhost permission and passed completely.
